Student pages
For professors

A proposal for faculty review: nothing changes in your course until it’s agreed.
Questions: reply to the email, or write to languagelab-gvl@ung.edu.

What changes

Same labs and Bongo recordings for every section type. Students find everything in one place, test their setup before the first lab, and are graded on one speaking rubric. Click a tile to see why; click again to turn it back.

Before→After

Structure

  • LAB folderBefore: A Start Here module plus a subfolder for each lab→After: One LAB folder, no subfolders: a tabbed description, Lab 0, then each lab's quiz and Bongo
  • InstructionsBefore: 3–4 pages per lab that sometimes disagree (3 or 5 prompts in Lab 1)→After: One set of instructions inside each Bongo assignment
  • DesignBefore: A different layout on each page→After: One layout everywhere: tabs, due-date chips, the current lab highlighted

Lab 0

  • Lab 0Before: Guidelines Quiz unlocks the labs→After: Lab 0: the Guidelines Quiz plus a one-minute Bongo camera + screen check, due before Lab 1. Both 0%
  • Keyboard demoBefore: Accent questions are multiple choice→After: A keyboard setup demo for Windows and Mac, then students type accented words

Deadlines

  • Due timeBefore: 5:00 PM in SPAN 1002 only→After: 5:00 PM in both courses

Recording

  • One video per labBefore: Question & Answer prompts, heard one at a time→After: One individual video, with every question written on the Bongo page
  • TroubleshootingBefore: One general list→After: Split into video labs and slide labs, each with one backup: a phone take, or a PowerPoint or Canva MP4
  • NotecardBefore: One card, up to 15 words→After: Same card, held to the camera for 5 seconds at the start

Grading

  • RubricBefore: Its own rubric→After: Fluency & Discourse 10 · Comprehensibility & Accuracy 5 · Vocabulary 5 · Task 5, plus a 0 column

Behind the scenes

  • New GitHub repositoryBefore: Instructions edited course by course→After: One repository for the lab pages, linked from every course, with one copy per campus
  • Course copyBefore: Copying a course brings last semester's lab items→After: Leave the lab items out; the Lab sets up fresh ones

Lab tasks

  • A cocinarAfter: Recorded on a phone and uploaded to Bongo.
  • Días festivosAfter: Preterite for regular sections; imperfect and preterite for Stone, which has already practiced the imperfect.
  • StoneAfter: Lab 2 is called La niñez instead of El repaso; Lab 1 drops the Chapter 7 grammar extras.
  • Recording in the LabAfter: Optional for in-person sections. Stone and online sections record on their own and can book tutoring.

What stays the same

  • Six labs (four in summer), 25 points each, graded by Language Lab staff.
  • Each lab is a mini-quiz plus a Bongo recording; face visible, Spanish only.
  • No face or no audio is 0 points with no resubmission. No late work apart from Excused Absences. The Guidelines Quiz (75%) still unlocks the labs, now together with Lab 0.

Student workflow

Students go from the announcement to one LAB folder, complete Lab 0 (the Guidelines Quiz and a Bongo setup check), then work through the labs in order. Click a step to see its page.

Previews show the Gainesville copy. Each campus gets its own copy that shows only its own Language Lab contact.

Troubleshooting

  1. What should you use to record in Bongo?

    • Correct: Google Chrome on a laptop or desktop
    • Safari on an iPhone

  2. The Bongo recorder won't load. What should you try? (Select all that apply.)

    • Correct: Clear Chrome's cache and cookies, then reload
    • Correct: Try a Chrome Incognito window
    • Correct: Restart your computer
    • Wait until after the deadline

  3. Recording in Bongo keeps failing. What else can you do?

    • Correct: Record one continuous take with your phone or camera app, then choose Upload Video
    • Email the video to your professor
    • Skip the lab

  4. In a slide lab, Bongo still can't share your screen. What can you upload instead?

    • Correct: A PowerPoint or Canva recording, exported as an MP4
    • A screen recording from any app
    • Photos of your slides

  5. In the cooking lab (A cocinar), you record on your phone. How do you turn it in?

    • Correct: In Bongo, choose Upload and select the video file
    • Email the video to the Language Lab
    • Record it again in Bongo

  6. How do you redo a recording before the due date?

    • Correct: Open the ⋮ menu and choose Reset Submission
    • Submit a second assignment
    • Ask the Lab to delete it

Lab 0 · part 2

Lab 0: Bongo setup check New

Lab 0 works like every lab: a quiz, then a Bongo recording. Part 1 is the Guidelines Quiz. Part 2 is this one-minute camera + screen recording with three PowerPoint slides, in the first week. Camera + screen is the hardest recording, so one test covers every lab.

For students

  • Unlimited tries, 0% of the grade.
  • Marked Complete or Not yet within one business day.
  • If screen sharing fails, they practice the fallback: a PowerPoint recording uploaded as an MP4.
  • Stays open all semester to test a new computer.

In D2L

  • Both parts are grade items in the Lab Assignments category, excluded from the final grade. The Bongo check is 1 point: Complete = 1.
  • Every lab quiz and Bongo assignment gets two release conditions: Guidelines Quiz ≥ 75% and Bongo setup check = 1.
  • Bongo needs a 0 option in the Lab 0 rubric (Not yet) to send a 0 to D2L.

Content › LAB › Lab 0 (Bongo)

Content › LAB

Mini-quizzes

Speaking rubric New

One rubric for every lab in both courses. Still 25 points, so course weights don't change. Speaking carries 60%, vocabulary has its own row, and Engagement is gone.

Fluency & Discourse 10Comprehensibility & Accuracy 5Vocabulary Range 5Task Completion 5

Fluency & Discourse 10 points

  1. Exceeds10Connected sentences joined with linking words; talks to the camera; pauses only to think.
  2. Meets8Mostly complete sentences with some linking words; pauses or restarts don't break the message.
  3. Approaches6A mix of sentences and fragments with long pauses, or flat, list-like delivery with eyes off the camera.
  4. Does not meet4Mostly single words or fragments with long silences, or recited for most of the video.
  5. Nothing to rate0The whole video can't be scored (see below).

Comprehensibility & Accuracy 5 points

  1. Exceeds5Easy to understand throughout; this lab's grammar used correctly.
  2. Meets4Understood without effort; this lab's grammar used with a few errors.
  3. Approaches3Needs a patient listener, or this lab's grammar is missing or often wrong.
  4. Does not meet2Hard to understand even after replaying.
  5. Nothing to rate0The whole video can't be scored (see below).

Vocabulary Range 5 points

  1. Exceeds5Varied: chapter words plus descriptive words and different verbs; rarely repeats; no English.
  2. Meets4Chapter vocabulary used correctly, with some variety and description.
  3. Approaches3A small set of words repeated; little description; some English.
  4. Does not meet2Very few words; frequent English or invented words.
  5. Nothing to rate0The whole video can't be scored (see below).

Task Completion 5 points

  1. Exceeds5Every part answered with specific details; meets the length.
  2. Meets4Every part answered; some answers brief; meets the length.
  3. Approaches3One part missing, or under the length.
  4. Does not meet2Two or more parts missing, or under half the length.
  5. Nothing to rate0The whole video can't be scored (see below).

Nothing to rate (0 in every row): no face or no audio for most of the video, mostly not Spanish, a different lab's task, an edited upload, or a video sent outside Bongo. Bongo needs this column to record a 0.

  • Notecard: students hold it up to the camera for about 5 seconds at the start. Sentences on the card or the slides: Fluency & Discourse is scored no higher than Does not meet. Rehearsed speech is fine; reading is scored as delivery, not as a separate penalty.
  • Slides not visible in a slide lab for most of the video (Bongo tab or wrong window shared): Task Completion is scored no higher than Does not meet (2). The speaking rows are scored as usual.
  • Labs with a video comment: a missing comment counts as one missing part in Task Completion.
  • Lab 0's Bongo setup check has no rubric: Complete or Not yet, worth 0% of the grade.

Copying your course to a new semester New

When you copy last semester's course into the new one, leave the lab items out. The Language Lab sets up the LAB folder, its files and the Bongo links in every new course. Copying last semester's lab items creates duplicates and Bongo links that point to old assignments.

  1. In the new course: Course Admin › Import / Export / Copy Components › Copy Components from another Org Unit. Search for your old course, then choose Select Components.

  2. Choose components: set them as shown, then choose Continue.

  3. D2L then shows one page for each component you set to individual items. On each page, uncheck the lab items:

    1. Select Content Modules and Topics: Uncheck the LAB folder. Its name depends on the section type; uncheck whichever shows. Continue.

    2. Select Course Files: Uncheck the lab files folder, whichever shows. Continue.

    3. External Learning Tool Links: Uncheck the lab links: the Bongo lab assignments and the Kaltura audio and video used in the lab quizzes. Keep any links of your own, such as your own Kaltura media. VHL comes preloaded, so you don't need to copy it. Continue.

    4. Grades: Uncheck the Lab Assignments category. Its grade items uncheck with it. Continue.

    5. Quizzes: Uncheck the lab quizzes. Continue.

  4. Finish the copy as usual.
